# noaa-apt

**Decoder for NOAA weather-satellite APT imagery**

> **Status: retired.** All NOAA APT satellites were taken out of service on 2025-11-09. The software is not broken; the signals it decodes no longer exist. Verified by us against NOAA service notices rather than inherited from AHRL's shell comment. Recorded 2025-11-09. Verdict tested by us.

- **Version recorded:** 1.4.1
- **Categories:** `satellite`, `sdr`
- **Upstream:** <https://noaa-apt.mbernardi.com.ar/>
- **Superseded by:** `satdump`
- **Not a recommended default** — installed only when asked for.

## What it does

Decodes Automatic Picture Transmission signals from NOAA weather satellites into visible and infrared images, from a recording or a live SDR feed.

## Why you would want it

You almost certainly do not, any more. Every NOAA satellite that transmitted APT was decommissioned on 2025-11-09. For weather imagery from satellites that are still transmitting, use SatDump, which handles current LRPT and HRPT services.

## Before it will work

An RTL-SDR or recorded audio of an APT pass.

## How it installs

- prebuilt zip from https://github.com/martinber/noaa-apt/releases/download/v1.4.1/noaa-apt-1.4.1-aarch64-linux-gnu.zip — *arch aarch64*
- prebuilt zip from https://github.com/martinber/noaa-apt/releases/download/v1.4.1/noaa-apt-1.4.1-x86_64-linux-gnu.zip — *arch x86_64*

## Known problems

Retired: the signal source is gone. Kept in the catalog so that operators searching for an APT decoder get this explanation instead of finding nothing and assuming we missed it.

## Keeping it current

- probe: none
- strategy: manual
- Retired. No further updates expected or wanted.
